Normalization: Native configuration-only captures; no payload, lifecycle scheduling, execution deadlines or worker latency is asserted.
Generated nonempty rule IDs are bound at their first native read and reused on retained-configuration reads; rule and transition array order is compared, not randomized IDs.
CLI timestamp strings are canonicalized to RFC3339 UTC Z for Go SDK JSON output; raw lexical timestamp cases preserve their native XML.
Three local CLI validation failures are evidence-only and excluded; native wire counterparts cover missing status, empty tag key and fractional Days.

SDK-representable requests use the generated Go client. Raw requests preserve native required-field rejection, lexical timestamps, fractional/overflowing integers and an explicit empty minimum-size header.

Native response headers/XML remain in evidence. Replay compares lifecycle transition-default header presence/value, exact modeled fields and meaningful omissions; empty successful control responses are proved by HTTP status, never a vacuous empty output.
Reopen on each generated-ID stability read is a local persistence projection only. Calls retain native request timestamps; empty buckets make time advancement immaterial.
Capture labels are probe intentions, not outcome claims: initial mixed legacy/Filter ordered-generated-ids request was rejected; valid homogeneous ordered/generated-ID scenarios are in supplement.

Seven immediate GET observations returned older accepted configurations, including temporary reversion after a current read and stale data immediately after successful DELETE; exclude these transient stale reads instead of implementing native propagation timing. All exact native responses remain in evidence.
The explicit empty minimum-size header uses captured raw XML because the Go SDK enum zero value omits that header.
Actual principal is IAM user Delegated, not root. Lifecycle config APIs in this owner-only replay use the existing local caller projection; caller-authority evidence is separate.
